Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Church life

forgiveness noun

also pardon, remission of sins, ask forgiveness, grant a pardon, obtain a pardon

classical

Traupman 196, 356
Cic. Rab. Perd. 5: ab Jove … pācem ac veniam petō (Lewis & Short)

venia, veniae f.

noun, first declension

forgiveness, pardon

Favour, and so pardon: veniam dare, to forgive; veniam petere, to ask forgiveness; veniam impetrāre, to obtain it (Traupman).

Other words

  • remissiō peccātōrum — the forgiveness of sins

    also used · late Latin · Vulg. Act. 2.38; Tert. Adv. Marc. 4.28 (Lewis & Short)

    The forgiveness of sins in the Vulgate and the Creed.

Examples

  • ōrō ut imprūdentiae dēs prīmum veniam

    first, please forgive my blundering inPhaedr. 4.21.5–6

  • hoc argūmentum veniam eī darī docet quī cāsū peccat

    this story teaches that forgiveness is given to the one who does wrong by accidentPhaedr. 5.3.11–12

  • Poenitentiam, inquit, agite, et baptīzētur ūnusquisque vestrum in nōmine Jēsū Chrīstī in remissiōnem peccātōrum vestrōrum

    Repent, he said, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sinsVulg. Act. 2.38

  • veniam alicui dare

    to grant someone a pardonTraupman 196

  • veniam impetrāre

    to obtain pardonTraupman 196

See also forgive, sin, repent, confession.

SourcesLewis & Short: venia · Lewis & Short: remissio
